intro: Adjectives that change meaning with their position, and what putting an adjective first does to a sentence.
p.viejo.nota: Un viejo amigo: a long-standing friend. Un amigo viejo: an elderly friend.
p.pobre.nota: Un pobre hombre: an unfortunate man. Un hombre pobre: a man with no money.
p.grande.nota: Before a singular noun it becomes gran: un gran escritor.
p.nuevo.nota: Un nuevo coche: another car. Un coche nuevo: a brand-new car.
p.antiguo.nota: Mi antiguo jefe: my former boss. Un mueble antiguo: an antique.
p.único.nota: Mi único hijo: my only child. Un hijo único: an only child. Una obra única: a unique work.
p.cierto.nota: Cierta noticia: a certain piece of news. Una noticia cierta: a true piece of news.
p.simple.nota: Un simple empleado: a mere employee. Un trabajo simple: a simple job.
p.medio.nota: Media hora: half an hour. El ciudadano medio: the average citizen.
p.mismo.nota: El mismo profesor: the same teacher. El profesor mismo: the teacher himself.
p.puro.nota: Por pura casualidad: by sheer chance. Agua pura: pure water.
b1.texto:
The normal place of a Spanish adjective is after the noun, and there it **distinguishes**: **un coche rojo** is red and not another colour.

Before the noun, an adjective does not distinguish. It **comments**: it adds an evaluation or something already known. That is why it sounds literary or emphatic: **un grave problema**, **la blanca nieve**, **una magnífica idea**.

Some adjectives must go after: those of nationality, colour, shape and type. You say **un producto lácteo**, **una chica francesa**, never the other way round.

A small group has two meanings. Before the noun the meaning is subjective, after it literal.
b2.nota: Grande becomes gran before any singular noun: un gran día, una gran idea.
b3.texto:
Suffixes turn a colour into an approximate one: rojo → **rojizo**; amarillo → **amarillento**; azul → **azulado**; verde → **verdoso**; blanco → **blanquecino**; negro → **negruzco**. They always go after the noun: **un cielo rojizo**.

An adjective can also describe the subject through the verb: **Ana llegó cansada.** **Los niños volvieron contentos.** It agrees with the subject, not with the verb.
b5.o0.refuerzo: Before the noun, antiguo means former.
b5.o1.refuerzo: That would be mi profesor, que es muy mayor.
b5.o2.refuerzo: Before the noun, antiguo means former.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence says the man has no money?
b6.o0.refuerzo: After the noun, pobre is literal.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Before the noun, pobre means unfortunate.
b7.pregunta: Complete: Cervantes was a great writer.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Grande shortens to gran before a singular noun, and means great.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Before a singular noun, grande shortens to gran.
b8.o0.refuerzo: After the noun, único means the only one of its kind in the family.
b8.o1.refuerzo: That would be es mi única hija.
b8.o2.refuerzo: The fixed phrase hijo único means only child.
b9.o0: I found out by sheer chance.
b9.o0.explicacion: Por pura casualidad means purely by chance, not through an agreed coincidence.
b9.o1: I found out through a pure coincidence.
b9.o1.explicacion: Before the noun, puro means sheer.
b9.o2: I knew it was a clean accident.
b10.pregunta: Complete: the children came back tired.
b10.o0.refuerzo: The adjective agrees with the subject, los niños.
b10.o1.refuerzo: It must agree with los niños: plural.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Spanish uses the adjective here, not an adverb.
b11.traduccion: He is an old friend of the family.
b12.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Describe someone you have known for many years and a place from your past, placing the adjectives carefully.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud the difference between pairs such as un viejo amigo and un amigo viejo, with your own examples.
